rule: **Zig**: file-qualified: `file.Struct#fn`, `file.fn`; `@import` bindings make `std.x.y` medium. | `self.m()` / `this.m()` / a bare call to a member of the enclosing type → `Type#m`. | Free function: its name (with the language's module qualifier where it has one).
notes: call_type convention used throughout this corpus: a callee that is a member of a type (`T#m`) or a receiver-qualified guess (`recv.m`, `.m`) is `method`; a free function (`file.f`, `std.x.f`) is `direct`. All files sit directly under src/, so the file qualifier is the basename (`app`, `util`). Every fn declared in a struct is `app.Point#fn` whether or not it takes self. `scale(...)` inside Point is a bare call to a member of the enclosing type → `app.Point#scale`; `self.len()` → `app.Point#len`. `Point.len(p)` (Type.m) and `p.len()` with `p: Point` declared both give `app.Point#len`. The struct literal `Point{ .x = 0, .y = 0 }` is data construction, `_ =` is a discard, `self.x` is field access: no edges.
